title: The Incarnation and Redemption
summary: The Incarnation is the mystery of the Son of God becoming truly man while remaining truly God, accomplishing our salvation through his life, death, and Resurrection. Redemption is the work by which Christ reconciled us to the Father, offering himself as the perfect sacrifice for our sins.

blocks.text: Introduction: The Word Became Flesh

With the Nicene Creed, the Church confesses that for us men and for our salvation, the Son of God came down from heaven, became incarnate by the Holy Spirit and the Virgin Mary, and was made man. This is the mystery of the Incarnation: the eternal Word of God assumed a human nature to accomplish our salvation in it. [CCC 456, 461]
And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, full of grace and truth; we have beheld his glory, glory as of the only Son from the Father.

blocks.title: CCC 461: The Incarnation
blocks.text: The Church calls Incarnation the fact that the Son of God assumed a human nature in order to accomplish our salvation in it.
I. Why the Word Became Flesh

The Word became flesh for us in order to save us by reconciling us with God, who loved us and sent his Son to be the expiation for our sins. The Father sent his Son as the Savior of the world, and he was revealed to take away sins. [CCC 457]

The Word became flesh so that we might know the depth of God's love for us. By sending his only Son as the Savior of the world, God manifested his love among us, so that we might live through him. [CCC 458]

In this the love of God was made manifest among us, that God sent his only Son into the world, so that we might live through him. In this is love, not that we loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the expiation for our sins.

The Word became flesh to be our model of holiness. Jesus invites his disciples to take up their cross and follow him, for he is the way, the truth, and the life. Through the Holy Spirit, he makes us sharers in his own life as the beloved Son. [CCC 459]

The Word became flesh to make us partakers of the divine nature. The Son of God became man so that we might become God, entering into communion with the Word and receiving divine sonship. The only-begotten Son assumed our nature so that he, made man, might make men gods. [CCC 460]

blocks.title: CCC 457-460: Four Reasons for the Incarnation
blocks.text: The Word became flesh to save us by reconciling us with God, that we might know God's love, to be our model of holiness, and to make us partakers of the divine nature.
II. True God and True Man

The unique and altogether singular event of the Incarnation does not mean that Jesus Christ is part God and part man, nor does it imply that he is the result of a confused mixture of the divine and the human. He became truly man while remaining truly God. Jesus Christ is true God and true man. [CCC 464]

Faced with various heresies, the fourth ecumenical council at Chalcedon (451) confessed one and the same Son, our Lord Jesus Christ: perfect in divinity and perfect in humanity, truly God and truly man, composed of rational soul and body; consubstantial with the Father as to his divinity and consubstantial with us as to his humanity. [CCC 467]
Who, though he was in the form of God, did not count equality with God a thing to be grasped, but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being born in the likeness of men.

The Council of Chalcedon teaches that one and the same Christ, Son, Lord, and only-begotten, is to be acknowledged in two natures without confusion, change, division, or separation. The distinction between the natures was never abolished by their union, but the character proper to each nature was preserved as they came together in one person and one hypostasis. [CCC 467]

blocks.title: CCC 464: Not Part God, Part Man
blocks.text: The Incarnation does not mean Christ is part God and part man, nor a confused mixture; he became truly man while remaining truly God.

blocks.title: CCC 480-481: One Person, Two Natures
blocks.text: Jesus Christ is true God and true man in the unity of his divine person, possessing two natures, one divine and one human, not confused but united in the one person of God's Son.
III. The Mystery of Redemption

Christ died for our sins in accordance with the scriptures. Our salvation flows from God's initiative of love for us, because he loved us and sent his Son to be the expiation for our sins. God shows his love for us in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us. [CCC 619-620]

Jesus freely offered himself for our salvation. During the Last Supper, he both symbolized this offering and made it really present, saying: This is my body which is given for you. The redemption won by Christ consists in this: he came to give his life as a ransom for many, loving his own to the end. [CCC 621-622]
For the Son of man also came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.

Christ's death is both the Paschal sacrifice that accomplishes the definitive redemption of men through the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world, and the sacrifice of the New Covenant which restores man to communion with God by reconciling him to God through the blood of the covenant poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins. [CCC 613]

blocks.title: CCC 613: Paschal Sacrifice
blocks.text: Christ's death is the Paschal sacrifice that accomplishes definitive redemption and the sacrifice of the New Covenant that restores communion with God.
IV. The Fruits of Redemption

There is not, never has been, and never will be a single human being for whom Christ did not suffer. Christ's sacrifice on the cross is the one perfect and complete sacrifice for the sins of all humanity, offered once for all. [CCC 605]

Jesus' violent death was not the result of chance or an unfortunate coincidence of circumstances, but part of the mystery of God's plan. The Scriptures foretold that the Messiah must suffer and rise from the dead, and Christ fulfilled these prophecies through his Passion, death, and Resurrection. [CCC 599-600]
But God shows his love for us in that while we were yet sinners Christ died for us.

All men are called to this union with Christ. The redemptive sacrifice of Christ is unique, accomplished once for all, yet it is made present in the celebration of the Eucharist and extends its saving power to all times and places. [CCC 618]

blocks.title: CCC 618: One Perfect Sacrifice
blocks.text: Christ's redemptive sacrifice is unique, accomplished once for all, yet made present in the Eucharist and extending its saving power to all times and places.
V. Our Response to the Gift of Salvation

The gift of salvation calls for our free response of faith and love. We are justified by faith in Christ and by the grace of God, not by our own works, yet faith works through love and produces good works as fruits of our union with Christ. [CCC 620]

By his glorious Cross, Christ has won salvation for all mankind. He redeemed them from the sin that held them captive, opening for them the way to union with God. In his Resurrection, he manifests the divine life he won for us through his death. [CCC 654]

I have been crucified with Christ; it is no longer I who live, but Christ who lives in me; and the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me.

The cross is the unique sacrifice of Christ, the high priest of the new and eternal covenant. Yet, because in his incarnate divine person he has in some way united himself to every man, the possibility of being made partners, in a way known to God, in the paschal mystery is offered to all men. [CCC 618]

blocks.title: CCC 620: God's Initiative of Love
blocks.text: Our salvation flows from God's initiative of love for us, because he loved us and sent his Son to be the expiation for our sins.

blocks.title: Closing Prayer: Anima Christi
blocks.text: Soul of Christ, sanctify me. Body of Christ, save me. Blood of Christ, inebriate me. Water from the side of Christ, wash me. Passion of Christ, strengthen me. O good Jesus, hear me. Within thy wounds hide me. Suffer me not to be separated from thee. From the malicious enemy defend me. In the hour of my death call me. And bid me come unto thee, that with thy saints I may praise thee, for ever and ever. Amen.

blocks.title: Prayer of Thanksgiving
blocks.text: We give you thanks, O Lord Jesus Christ, for your Incarnation and Redemption. You became man to save us, died for our sins, and rose to give us new life. Grant that we may always live in your love and share in your divine nature. Amen.
